Geographic focus:
Global (primary focus: United States, with secondary focus on Europe, Japan, Middle East/Jordan-Iran conflict)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references August monthly performance, historical September weakness
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — September Fed rate hike, ECB meeting Sep 9-10, payrolls report, CPI Sep 11
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
Risk-off session on Aug 31, 2026 driven by a U.S.-Iran military escalation (U.S. strikes on Larak Island, Iranian missile retaliation at U.S. bases in Jordan), surging oil prices (Brent +2.71% to $90.49, WTI +2.83% to $85.76), and a sharply repriced Fed rate hike path. Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech pushed September hike odds from ~35% to 65%. Equities sold off (Dow -0.70%, S&P -0.33%, Nasdaq -0.12%), 10Y Treasury yields rose to 4.758%, while the dollar softened. The yen firmed on BOJ rate hike signals. Key near-term catalysts: August payrolls (Friday) and CPI (Sep 11).

---

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES — The article centers on the Fed rate hike repricing, rising Treasury yields, and their knock-on effects on equities and FX, with the geopolitical shock acting as an inflationary accelerant to that core narrative.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly YES)
Probability of increase: 65% (explicitly stated via fed funds futures pricing for September hike)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (marginally, only as the prior baseline before Warsh's speech)
Probability of holding: 35% (implied residual, down sharply from ~65% pre-Warsh)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — no mention of cuts; directional bias is entirely toward hikes)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 75 (Meaningfully MORE HAWKISH than before — Warsh's Jackson Hole speech has materially shifted rate hike expectations, oil-driven inflation risk compounds the hawkish tilt, and 10Y yields are pressing multi-month highs. No dovish offset present.)
